text:
maria-cs: Hey team, getting escalated from Acme — their rerank endpoint is returning crazy numbers, negative values and some >1.0. They expected scores in [0,1]. Can someone explain?

nina-support: Oof. Any sample payload or response they sent?

maria-cs: Pasted below (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  \"query\": \"best travel credit card\",
  \"candidates\": [\"card A\", \"card B\", \"card C\"],
  \"top_k\": 3,
  \"client_id\": \"acme-prod-12\"
}
```

Response snippet: `[{"id":"card A","score":-2.137},{"id":"card B","score":0.45},{"id":"card C","score":3.1}]`

leo-ml: This matches a common confusion: the rerank endpoint currently returns raw model logits by default (not normalized probabilities). Logits can be negative or >1.0 — that doesn't mean output is broken. We should call this out in docs.

sam-platform: Confirming — internal flag `normalize_scores` exists but isn't exposed in hosted API yet (we kept it for internal evals). For public API we return raw scores to avoid misleading consumers who want to apply custom calibration.

maria-cs: Client insists this is a bug because their frontend expects 0..1 and used scores directly. They're asking for guidance and quick fix.

leo-ml: Short guidance we can give: 1) Treat scores as logits. 2) If you want normalized probabilities, apply softmax over candidate scores on the client side. 3) If comparing across queries, you must calibrate or use rank-only metrics.

nina-support: Can you drop a tiny repro snippet for them to run? Prefer JS/Python both.

leo-ml: Sure. Python example: 
```
import math
scores = [-2.137, 0.45, 3.1]
# softmax -> probs
exps = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exps) for e in exps]
print(probs)
```
JS equivalent: 
```
const scores = [-2.137, 0.45, 3.1];
const exps = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s));
const sum = exps.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
const probs = exps.map(e=>e/sum);
console.log(probs);
```

sam-platform: Also note: if the client is doing batching/padding and then averaging scores across batches, padding tokens or candidate ordering can change logits. Ask them to send exact request body and server time window so we can correlate logs.

maria-cs: They also mentioned occasional 400 for large candidate lists, saying the problem started after they increased candidates >100. Could that be related?

sam-platform: Yes — we enforce a candidate limit per request (100) at the gateway. When they truncated/paginated client-side, they might have changed candidate ordering or tokenization which affects logits. 400 would be a separate issue (we return 413/400 depending on payload). Provide them the limit and suggest chunking with deterministic ordering.

nina-support: Action items for reply to client: 1) Explain raw logits vs probabilities + include softmax snippets; 2) Recommend deterministic ordering and respecting candidate limit (<=100) or use batching; 3) Offer a temporary server-side normalization option (we can flip normalize_scores for them on dedicated/private) or we can post-process results in response if they want — but this is manual; 4) Ask for their exact request/headers and a sample request_id/timestamp so eng can grep logs.

leo-ml: I'll draft a small blurb we can paste into the ticket about score semantics and calibration pitfalls. Also: suggest they evaluate rank metrics (MRR/NDCG) instead of raw score magnitudes.

maria-cs: Draft looks good. Pasting the snippet we will send to the client (editable):

---paste start---
Heads up: Rerank scores are model logits (raw scores). These are not probabilities and can be negative or greater than 1. If you need probabilities, convert via softmax over candidates. Example code attached. If your frontend assumes 0..1, that will produce misleading UX. Also confirm you are sending candidates in the correct order and under the per-request candidate limit (100). If you'd like, we can enable server-side normalization for your Dedicated instance or help you add a small post-processing step.
---paste end---

nina-support: Small edit: add explicit note that per-query softmax is the right approach for converting to a distribution.

maria-cs: Sent to client. They replied with permission to enable server-side normalization on Dedicated — they said they'll consider Dedicated but want a quick client-side workaround for now.

sam-platform: I'll open an internal ticket (infra) to track adding an optional `normalize=true` query param in the hosted API; ETA: needs product signoff. In the meantime, raising a docs PR to make the current behavior explicit.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: docs/rerank-score-clarity.md -> staging

leo-ml: One more note for the thread: if you need reproducible ranking scores across model versions, don't compare raw logits across checkpoints — calibrate or use a rescorer trained to output probabilities.

maria-cs: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up in the support ticket with repro steps we asked for and the softmax snippet. Marking this thread resolved for CS side. :white_check_mark:
